def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    import numpy as np
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n_steps = 60
    dt = duration_s / (n_steps - 1)
    points = np.empty((n_runs, n_steps, 3), dtype=float)
    points[:, 0, :2] = start
    points[:, 0, 2] = 0.0
    ok = np.ones(n_runs, dtype=bool)

    lat = np.full(n_runs, start[0])
    lon = np.full(n_runs, start[1])
    time = np.zeros(n_runs)

    m_lat = terrain.m_lat
    m_lon = terrain.m_lon
    cell = terrain.cell_m

    for i in range(1, n_steps):
        # Sample bearings near ridge direction: estimate steepest ascent direction by slope gradients
        # Approximate gradient by small offsets
        delta = cell / 111111  # degrees approx per meter lat
        lat_up = lat + delta
        lat_dn = lat - delta
        lon_up = lon + delta / np.cos(np.deg2rad(lat))
        lon_dn = lon - delta / np.cos(np.deg2rad(lat))

        elev_c = terrain.elev(lat, lon)
        elev_up = terrain.elev(lat_up, lon)
        elev_dn = terrain.elev(lat_dn, lon)
        elev_l = terrain.elev(lat, lon_dn)
        elev_r = terrain.elev(lat, lon_up)

        grad_lat = (elev_up - elev_dn) / (2 * cell)  # m/m
        grad_lon = (elev_r - elev_l) / (2 * cell)  # m/m approx

        # ridge azimuth approximated orthogonal to gradient (max elevation gain direction)
        ridge_bearing = np.arctan2(-grad_lat, grad_lon)  # perpendicular to grad vector

        # Add some noise to bearings to explore locally higher points
        bearing = ridge_bearing + rng.normal(0, np.pi/6, n_runs)  # ±30 deg noise

        # Try multiple step lengths modulated by slope and speed:
        slope = terrain.slope_deg(lat, lon)
        step_dist = cell * (0.5 + 0.5 * rng.uniform(size=n_runs))  # 15 to 30 m

        # Calculate candidate new points:
        lat_new, lon_new = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearing, step_dist)

        # Clamp new points inside terrain
        lat_new, lon_new = terrain.clamp(lat_new, lon_new)

        # Calculate elevation difference and horizontal distance for speed
        elev_new = terrain.elev(lat_new, lon_new)
        d_elev = elev_new - elev_c
        d_horiz = step_dist

        speed = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(d_elev, d_horiz)
        # constrain speed ≥ 0.1 m/s to avoid division by zero or too slow
        speed = np.maximum(speed, 0.1)

        # Calculate actual time step, may be longer or shorter than dt depending on speed
        t_step = d_horiz / speed

        # If time + t_step > total duration per run, scale step back
        mask = time + t_step > duration_s
        if np.any(mask):
            scale = (duration_s - time[mask]) / t_step[mask]
            scale = np.clip(scale, 0, 1)
            # Re-calc lat,lon for these with scaled distance
            dist_scaled = step_dist[mask] * scale
            lat_s, lon_s = terrain.offset(lat[mask], lon[mask], bearing[mask], dist_scaled)
            lat_new[mask] = lat_s
            lon_new[mask] = lon_s
            t_step[mask] = duration_s - time[mask]

        time += t_step
        lat, lon = lat_new, lon_new

        points[:, i, 0] = lat
        points[:, i, 1] = lon
        points[:, i, 2] = time

        inside = terrain.inside(lat, lon)
        ok &= inside
        # once outside, fix point positions to last valid inside and time capped
        outside = ~inside
        if np.any(outside):
            # keep last valid position and time for the rest steps
            lat[outside] = lat_new[outside]
            lon[outside] = lon_new[outside]

    # Ensure monotonic time along each run axis (sanity)
    np.maximum.accumulate(points[:, :, 2], axis=1, out=points[:, :, 2])

    # Enforce start point at t=0 exactly
    points[:, 0, 0] = start[0]
    points[:, 0, 1] = start[1]
    points[:, 0, 2] = 0.

    return points, ok
